title: New Spectacles for a Growing Myope

patient.name: Master Nicholas Tan Wei Jie
patient.presenting_complaint: New patient referral — increasing difficulty seeing the whiteboard, query increase in spectacle power

history.hpc: Nicholas has worn glasses for myopia since age 9. Over the past 6 months, his teachers have moved him to the front of the class, but he still finds it hard to read the whiteboard clearly. His mother feels his current glasses, prescribed about 18 months ago, may no longer be strong enough. He is a new patient at this clinic today and has been sent for auto-refraction and auto-keratometry before seeing the doctor.
history.pmhx: Myopia since age 9, progressive. No previous eye surgery. No known ocular disease.
history.family_hx: Both parents wear glasses for myopia
history.social_hx: Secondary school student. Spends 2-3 hours daily on near work (homework, phone, tablet).

examination_findings.fundus: Not assessed today — new patient, to be reviewed by doctor

auto_refraction.comparison_to_old_glasses: Old glasses: RE -3.50 DS, LE -3.00 DS — increase in myopia of approximately -0.75 D each eye

diagnosis: Auto-refraction and auto-keratometry completed. Results suggest progression of myopia of approximately -0.75 D in each eye compared to current spectacles, consistent with the reported difficulty seeing the whiteboard. For doctor's review and subjective refraction to confirm new prescription.

immediate: Confirm patient identity and ask whether he is wearing glasses or contact lenses today
Ask patient to remove glasses (he is not wearing contact lenses) before testing
Perform hand hygiene and wipe machine chin rest and forehead rest with alcohol wipes
Position patient comfortably at the auto-refractor/keratometer with chin on rest and forehead against the bar
Instruct patient to open both eyes wide and look at the fixation target (e.g. a hot air balloon image) without squeezing eyes
Perform AR and AK as per doctor's order, taking repeat readings if values are inconsistent
Wipe machine contact parts with alcohol wipes after the procedure and perform hand hygiene
Document AR and AK readings for both eyes, and record VA with current glasses for comparison
Hand results to doctor for subjective refraction
follow_up: Doctor to perform subjective refraction to confirm final spectacle prescription
If significant myopia progression confirmed, doctor may discuss myopia control options (e.g. atropine drops, orthokeratology) given his age
New spectacle prescription to be dispensed if confirmed
patient_education: Explain that this machine gives the doctor a starting point — the doctor will still check his vision with different lenses to find the exact prescription
Advise on the 20-20-20 rule for near work: every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds
Encourage outdoor time, which has been shown to help slow myopia progression in children and teenagers

key_points: Confirms patient identity and asks patient to remove glasses before testing
Confirms patient is not wearing contact lenses
Asks about duration and progression of symptoms (difficulty seeing whiteboard, time since last prescription)
Notes family history of myopia and high near-work load as relevant context
Performs hand hygiene and wipes machine contact parts with alcohol wipes before and after
Positions patient correctly with both eyes open, looking at fixation target
Performs AR and AK for both eyes and takes repeat readings if inconsistent
Records AR and AK readings clearly for both eyes, plus VA with current correction
Recognises that AR/AK provides an objective starting estimate, not the final prescription
Compares AR result to old spectacle prescription to identify the degree of myopic progression
Does not finalise the new prescription independently — refers to doctor for subjective refraction
Identifies this as a case of progressive myopia in an adolescent
Documents AR/AK results and VA findings accurately and completely
Hands results to doctor for subjective refraction
Provides appropriate patient education on near-work habits and outdoor time for myopia control
Maintains correct infection control (alcohol wipes, hand hygiene) before and after the procedure
